text: We evaluated a weak-to-strong generalization method based on randomly dropping a fraction of weak labels each epoch, tested on the ethics_justice testbed across 5 seeds. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.57. Because no baseline PGR was supplied in the data provided, this number cannot be interpreted as an improvement over, or a regression from, any comparison condition; it stands only as a standalone measurement of the method under this configuration. Likewise, no standard error or per-seed spread was reported alongside the aggregate, so the seed-to-seed variability of the 0.57 figure is unknown and we cannot characterize how tightly the estimate is bounded. The finding is also limited to a single testbed, so it says nothing about whether label dropping transfers to other task domains. A useful next step would be to report the baseline PGR and the across-seed dispersion so the effect of the intervention can be assessed directly.
